term: terminus, cycle and endless support below a bearer
definition: `SupportTerminus m R Dependent w b x`: x is an existing support-ancestor of b with no existing direct supporter at w and fails `Dependent`. `SupportCycleBelow`: some ancestor of b reaches itself by one or more support edges. `EndlessSupportBelow`: some set contains b, contains only ancestors of b, and gives each member an existing direct supporter in the set. `BearerOutcome` is the disjunction of: accessibility with a terminus satisfying `Substance`; accessibility with a terminus failing it; a cycle; an endless set with no cycle. A terminus is a root of R at w only; a terminus failing `Substance` is not thereby a process or event.
note: Stipulated for #562. The set form of endlessness avoids the choice principle that extracting a sequence needs; a cycle gives a finite such set. See docs/notes/bearer-regress.md.
